dimensions.assessment: Affects individual taxpayers who receive math or clerical error notices from the IRS.
Provides more detailed, transparent information and simpler abatement procedures for tax adjustments, which is helpful administratively but does not fundamentally change tax liability rules.
dimensions.evidence: describe the mathematical or clerical error in comprehensive, plain language

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue changes are explicitly stated beyond administrative implementation and a pilot program.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 regarding notice contents, pilot programs, and abatement procedures.
dimensions.evidence: Section 6213(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to IRS notice requirements, taking effect for notices sent 12 months after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to notices sent after the date which is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Exact figures on how many taxpayers receive math or clerical error notices annually
Specific cost estimates for implementing the pilot program
importance_detail.rationale: The bill updates Internal Revenue Service procedures regarding math and clerical error notices and abatements, affecting taxpayers who receive such notices and IRS administrative processes.
